exposure: Factors influencing spontaneous cephalic version (e.g., multiparity, maternal age, polyhydramnios)
Cephalic presentation after external cephalic version (ECV)
outcome: Maternal and neonatal outcomes at delivery
cohort: Pregnant women with a breech fetus identified at their third-trimester ultrasound scan (around 32 weeks gestation) who were under the care of a tertiary hospital between 2003 and 2022.
finding: The study found a 65% spontaneous cephalic version rate, with multiparity, maternal age under 25, and polyhydramnios identified as favoring factors, and no difference in cesarean section or assisted vaginal delivery rates between spontaneous and ECV-achieved cephalic presentations.
mod_finding: There was no difference in the incidence of cesarean section or assisted vaginal delivery between fetuses that spontaneously turned cephalic and those that turned cephalic after external cephalic version.
gest_age: Around 32 weeks gestation at baseline, with follow-up until 36-37 weeks for version rate.
